metadata.name: bisik
metadata.description: Bisik: private stake-backed builder sourcing market

instructions.name: add_option
docs: Scouts add teams as options. Only a commitment to the team reference is stored;
the plaintext reference stays encrypted at the server (privacy matrix, living doc 7).

instructions.name: allocate_position
docs: Fold one position's encrypted option into the encrypted aggregate (sequential, one at a time).

instructions.name: buy_flat
docs: Non-winning verified buyers buy the remaining signals at the flat price.

instructions.name: claim
docs: Scout claims refundable stake + payout to any recipient, proving ownership of the
position's nullifier with a fresh Semaphore proof (same scope, message = recipient).

instructions.name: close_submit
docs: Close the submit window (F3). All positions must already be allocated.

instructions.name: compute_weights
docs: F9 step 1: reveal, per buyer, the total weight of that buyer's successful options.

instructions.name: init_auction_state
docs: Queue the zeroed encrypted auction state (auction markets only).

instructions.name: init_market_state
docs: Queue the zeroed encrypted aggregate for a market (must run before stakes are allocated).

instructions.name: open_bid
docs: Sealed bid, step 1 (F4): deposit the public ceiling (D-23) and open a bid record.

instructions.name: open_dispute
docs: F8: a buyer flags a verifiable claim in a position's reason as false, with evidence.

instructions.name: pay_team_share
docs: Team share (D-08, 5%) for buyer i, paid to the deploy wallet of an opted-in successful option.

instructions.name: place_bid
docs: Sealed bid, step 2: the encrypted amount is folded into the top-3 inside MPC and
capped at the deposited ceiling. The bidder identity is the signer (not user-supplied).

instructions.name: publish_group_root
docs: Operator publishes the Merkle root of an anonymous tier group (D-17).
The tree is built offchain from public leaves (identity commitments).

instructions.name: record_outcome
docs: F7: a successful outcome for (buyer, option). Grants are attested by the buyer;
deploys on Solana are attested by the operator's oracle (trust assumption, disclosed).

instructions.name: register_deploy_wallet
docs: Team opt-in (D-09): the operator registers the team's deploy wallet after the team claims it.

instructions.name: register_source_nullifier
docs: One source account (e.g. one GitHub account) = one scout (D-16). Only the hash is stored.

instructions.name: request_preview
docs: Reveal only the strength histogram (F4 preview), never option identities.

instructions.name: resolve_dispute
docs: Operator decides in v1. Upheld = proven hoax: the stake goes to charity (D-07);
losing opinions are never slashed.

instructions.name: select_hidden
docs: F5: winners hide up to x signals each, strictly in rank order (#1 then #2).

instructions.name: set_default_outcome
docs: D-05 default rule: a buyer who marked nothing gets the option with the strongest
signal they bought. The operator computes it from the decrypted signal view (disclosed).

instructions.name: settle_bid
docs: After resolution: losers get their full ceiling back; winners get ceiling − price,
and their price joins the scouts' pool as a buyer pool entry.

instructions.name: settle_position
docs: F9 step 2: per position, reveal only whether its option is in each buyer's
success set, then compute the payout in plaintext.

instructions.name: skip_selection
docs: Anyone may skip a winner who did not select before the deadline.

instructions.name: stake
docs: Anonymous stake (F2). Verifies a Semaphore membership proof for the tier group,
binds it to the stake payload, enforces one nullifier per (market, slot ≤ 3),
and escrows the refundable USDC stake. The supported option stays encrypted.

instructions.name: withdraw_fees
docs: Platform fee (D-08, 15%) to the treasury after settlement.

errors.name: Busy
errors.msg: Encrypted state busy; wait for the pending computation

errors.name: NotVisible
errors.msg: Option not visible to this buyer

errors.name: MissingOutcome
errors.msg: Every buyer needs at least one outcome (or a default)

types.name: AggState
docs: Encrypted per-option weighted support. Layout is fixed: see `ENC_OFFSET`.

types.name: AllocateOutput
docs: The output of the callback instruction. Provided as a struct with ordered fields
as anchor does not support tuples and tuple structs yet.

types.name: AuctionEnc
docs: Encrypted top-3 bids. Layout is fixed: see `ENC_OFFSET`.

types.name: ClockAccount
docs: An account storing the current network epoch

types.name: ComputationDefinitionAccount
docs: An account representing a [ComputationDefinition] in a MXE.

types.name: ComputationDefinitionMeta
docs: A computation definition for execution in a MXE.

types.name: ComputationSignature
docs: The signature of a computation defined in a [ComputationDefinition].

types.name: Epoch
docs: The network epoch

types.name: InitAuctionOutput
docs: The output of the callback instruction. Provided as a struct with ordered fields
as anchor does not support tuples and tuple structs yet.

types.name: InitMarketAggOutput
docs: The output of the callback instruction. Provided as a struct with ordered fields
as anchor does not support tuples and tuple structs yet.

types.name: LeaderChoice
docs: The computation chosen by a node to be executed when the node is leader.

types.name: LeaderInfo
docs: The information about a node.

types.name: LeaderSelector
docs: To select a Leader.
Uses the greatest divisors method: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/D%27Hondt_method

types.name: MXEAccount
docs: A MPC Execution Environment.

types.name: MxeStatus
docs: The status of an MXE.

types.name: NodeMetadata
docs: location as [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://www.iso.org/iso-3166-country-codes.html) country code

types.name: NodeRef
docs: A reference to a node in the cluster.
The offset is to derive the Node Account.

types.name: Output
docs: An output of a computation.
We currently don't support encrypted outputs yet since encrypted values are passed via
data objects.

types.name: Parameter
docs: A parameter of a computation.
We differentiate between plaintext and encrypted parameters and data objects.
Plaintext parameters are directly provided as their value.
Encrypted parameters are provided as an offchain reference to the data.
Data objects are provided as a reference to the data object account.

in our case). Once all participants have set the value, the value is considered set and we only
store it once.
